WITH rep_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    e.EmployeeId,
    e.City,
    COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count
  FROM Employee e
  INNER JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City
),
city_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    City,
    AVG(customer_count) as avg_count
  FROM rep_counts
  GROUP BY City
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    rc.EmployeeId,
    rc.City,
    rc.customer_count,
    ca.avg_count
  FROM rep_counts rc
  JOIN city_avg ca ON rc.City = ca.City
  WHERE rc.customer_count > ca.avg_count
),
global_total AS (
  SELECT SUM(customer_count) as total FROM above_avg
)
SELECT 
  aa.City,
  SUM(aa.customer_count) as total_customers,
  AVG(aa.customer_count - aa.avg_count) as avg_excess,
  AVG(aa.customer_count / gt.total) as avg_share
FROM above_avg aa
CROSS JOIN global_total gt
GROUP BY aa.City

assumptions.assumption: Employees with NULL City values are included in city groupings; cities are compared and returned as-is without filtering NULLs
